## Upstream changes 4.4.1 -> 4.4.2

**Verdict:** SAFE TO APPLY — the only change is a Go toolchain upgrade for a CVE fix; no provider behaviour, resource schema, or variable changes are noted.

Note: the registry image data for `hashicorp/tls` could not be read (401 Unauthorized), so the usual cross-check against actual container configuration (user, entrypoint, command, ports, volumes, healthcheck, environment) was not possible. This does not change the verdict here since `hashicorp/tls` is a Terraform provider binary, not a service container with runtime configuration of that kind — but it is worth noting the registry check did not run.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes. The 4.4.2 entry contains only a NOTES item: "Upgrade the Go toolchain to 1.26.10 to mitigate the eMudhra certificate authority vulnerability (CVE-2026-111943)."

### Variables
- none. No provider schema, attribute, or `.env.example` variables are touched by this release.

### Data and dependencies
- none introduced by this range. No database, cache, or companion service is referenced by this provider or its notes.
- Already true at 4.4.1 (baseline, not a change in this upgrade): the 4.4.1 release itself was also just a Go toolchain bump ("Upgrade the Go toolchain to 1.26.8"), so the template was already running a provider built with a recent Go toolchain before this upgrade.

### Before applying
- None required beyond the normal `terraform init -upgrade` to pick up the new provider build. The compose/Terraform version constraint `version = "~> 4.4.1"` in `01-providers.tf` permits 4.4.2 automatically (pessimistic constraint operator allows patch-level upgrades), so no file edit is needed unless you want to pin the patch explicitly.
- No backup or state migration is implied: nothing in the notes touches resources, attributes, or state representation.

### Notes read
- hashicorp/terraform-provider-tls CHANGELOG.md, entries for v4.4.2 (2026-10-21) and v4.4.1 (2026-09-10, baseline).

## Upstream changes 6.69.1 -> 6.70.0

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — a breaking change in `aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record` import ID format, plus the registry check itself could not be performed.

The image configuration comparison could not be read: "The image configurations could not be read from the registry (HTTPError: HTTP Error 401: Unauthorized). Nothing below is measured; judge on the notes alone and say so." This review therefore rests on the release notes alone for user, entrypoint, command, ports, volumes, healthcheck and environment — none of which apply meaningfully to a Terraform provider binary anyway, but the absence of a verified image diff is noted as required.

### Breaking changes
- `resource/aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record`: "Change the format of the import ID from `domain_name,dnssec_key_id` to `domain_name,flags,algorithm,public_key`." Any existing `terraform import` commands, scripts, or documentation referencing the old ID format for this resource will fail. This only matters if the template's Route 53 domain configuration uses this resource.

### Variables
- none found in the notes or in `01-providers.tf` / `.env.example`. The provider version constraint is `version = "~> 6.69.1"`, which already permits 6.70.0 under the `~>` pessimistic operator (allows any 6.69.x, 6.70.x, ... up to <7.0.0 — actually `~> 6.69.1` only allows 6.69.x releases ≥ 6.69.1, so 6.70.0 is **not** satisfied by this constraint; it will need to be bumped, e.g. to `~> 6.70.0` or a broader range, for Terraform to pick up the new version).

### Data and dependencies
- none found regarding companion services (database, cache, search engine) — this provider manages AWS resources via API calls, not a pinned backend engine, so the "companion service version" rule does not apply here.
- No irreversible migrations, removed defaults, or changed ports/paths are mentioned in the notes for this range.

### Before applying
- Update the version constraint in `01-providers.tf` from `version = "~> 6.69.1"` to allow 6.70.0 (e.g. `~> 6.70.0` or `>= 6.69.1, < 7.0.0`), then run `terraform init -upgrade`.
- If the deployment manages any `aws_route53domains_delegation_signer_record` resources that were imported under the old ID scheme, re-import them using the new format `domain_name,flags,algorithm,public_key` before running further `terraform import` operations on them. Existing state for already-applied (non-imported) resources is unaffected by this format change per the bug-fix note for the same resource in this release.
- Take a state backup (`terraform state pull > backup.tfstate` or rely on the S3/DynamoDB backend's versioning once enabled) before applying, as routine practice for any provider bump.

### Notes read
- v6.70.0 (2026-10-21) release notes and CHANGELOG.md entry for 6.70.0
- v6.69.1 (2026-10-15) baseline release notes, given only as the starting point, not as a change in this range

## Upstream changes 2.45.2 -> 2.45.3

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — the notes carry a breaking change around trust of TLS certificates issued by a compromised CA, which can lock out SSO/LDAP authentication after the upgrade; no companion-service version requirement is introduced, and the image-level diff confirms no container-config change.

### Breaking changes
- "Portainer no longer trusts TLS certificates issued by eMudhra (emSign), following the compromise of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs (CVE-2026-111943). Connections to services that present an affected certificate, including OAuth/OIDC and LDAPS providers, registries and Git hosts, will fail after the upgrade. If your single sign-on or LDAP provider is affected, only the initial admin will be able to sign in. Check your services before upgrading."
- Related: "Removed the eMudhra emSign root certificates from the CA bundle in Linux images, and rejected certificate chains that contain the compromised eMudhra intermediates (CVE-2026-111943)."
- "Restricted kubeconfig tokens to the /api/endpoints/{id}/kubernetes proxy, so they are rejected with a 403 on every other API route, including admin-only routes and the Docker proxy. Kubeconfigs downloaded after upgrading carry a separate token per environment, limited to that environment" — not relevant to this template (no Kubernetes environments configured here), but worth knowing if the operator later connects one.

### Variables
- none — no compose or .env.example variable is renamed, removed, or newly required by this release.

### Data and dependencies
- none — the notes name no database, cache, or other companion-service version requirement for this range. (The compose file has no such companion service for Portainer itself; `traefik` and `backups` are unaffected by this image's release notes.)

### Before applying
- Check whether your OAuth/OIDC provider, LDAPS provider, container registries, or Git hosting use certificates issued through eMudhra/emSign intermediates. If any do, replace or re-issue those certificates before upgrading, since after the upgrade only the initial admin account will be able to sign in if SSO/LDAP breaks.
- No database migration, backup step, or config edit is called for beyond the operator's standard pre-upgrade backup (the `backups` service in this compose already covers that on its normal schedule — verify a recent backup exists before upgrading as routine practice).

### Notes read
- 2.45.3 (2026-10-21) — target version, read in full.
- 2.45.2 (2026-10-08) — baseline version, read for context only; its listed fixes/features are already in effect and not part of this upgrade's delta.
